div.head: Rect 4
div.ab: [4] Gebures gerihte. Geburgerihta syn mislice: gehwar hy syn hefige, gehwar eac medeme.
De geburi consuetudine. Geburi consuetudines inueniuntur multimode et ubi sunt onerose et ubi sunt (leuiores aut) medie.
GEBVRES GE|RIHTE . Gebur gerihta syn mislice . gehwar hy syn hefige . gehwar eac mederne .
Gebures gerihte Geburgerihta syn mislice: gehwar hy syn hefige; gehwar eac medeme.
Des Bauern Rechtspflichten. Bauernrechtspflichten sind verschieden: an einem Ort sind sie schwer, anderswo auch mässig.
4. The gebur's duties. The gebur's duties vary: in one place they are heavy, elsewhere also moderate.
The duty of the peasant The duties of the peasant are diverse, in some places they might be heavier, elsewhere [more] moderate.
The Duty of the Tenant Farmer The tenant farmer’s duties vary: in some places they are heavy; likewise, in others they are moderate.
div.note: K: ‘hefige,’ supplied from Liebermann, where it had dropped out. Liebermann notes that the customs of Tidenham continue here: ‘Se gebur sceal his riht don: he sceal erian healfne æcer to wiceworce …’.; AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 318, October 2026 (was “∅”, now “|”); AX: pages in Rabin (text / translation), checked against Rabin (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “318”, now “318 / 319”; 2 rows of Rect)
tenant farmer’s duties: That is, a tenant of peasant status whose rental included both homestead and farmland.
Candlemas: February 2, also referred to as the Feast of the Purification of the Virgin.

Vgl. Gl Bauer 4c-f. Der gebur steht, wie ceorl, oft im Ggs. zu þeow Urk. Birch 599; a. 995 Thorpe Dipl. 533. Er ist im 11. Jh. nicht mehr freizügig; Earle Landchar. 275. In Glossen steht er für colonus, vicinus; Sweet Old. texts 46; im Domesday steht gebur als Glosse über colibertus; diese beiden identifiziert Maitland Domesday 386. Persönlich ist er frei, aber er sitzt auf Zinsland (o. Urk. a. 995), nach dessen Areal er yardling heisst. Noch im 13. Jh. kommt er als burus, buriman vor; Vinogradoff Vill. 145. Er steht nicht etwa unter dem Kötter, wie Leo 118 denkt

Cf. Gl Bauer 4c-f. The gebur, like the ceorl, is often contrasted with the þeow: charter Birch 599; a. 995 Thorpe Dipl. 533. In the 11th cent. he no longer has freedom of movement; Earle Landchar. 275. In glosses he stands for colonus, vicinus; Sweet Old. texts 46; in Domesday gebur appears as a gloss above colibertus; Maitland Domesday 386 identifies these two. He is personally free, but he sits on rent-paying land (above, charter a. 995), after the extent of which he is called yardling. As late as the 13th cent. he still appears as burus, buriman; Vinogradoff Vill. 145. He by no means ranks below the cottar, as Leo 118 thinks
